Replay

Replay Hello and Loot views

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
HelloLootValidation

New Godot scenes built on Replay. The original hello_net, hello_sim, Cavecrawl, and Scrapyard projects remain in their original locations. These Hello and Loot scenes remain offline; the separate Network scene now uses the new server/client/observer runner.

From the repository root:

Shell
# Interactive Hello: arrows move, Space/Enter fires, Escape restarts.
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/play.sh

# Interactive loot: Space corrects the predicted winner, Escape restarts.
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/play.sh loot

# Builds both scenes and exercises real Godot processes headlessly.
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/run.sh

# Four-process networking gate, including injected 240 ms round-trip latency.
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/network_run.sh

# Interactive network host, then join from another terminal.
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/play.sh network
REPLAY_ROLE=client nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/play.sh network

The Network scene accepts REPLAY_ROLE=host|server|client|observer, REPLAY_PORT, REPLAY_ADDRESS, and receive-delay REPLAY_LATENCY (milliseconds). server is an avatarless authority; host has a local player. REPLAY_TOKEN provides a deterministic identity label for tests; normal clients generate random credentials. Persistence across app restarts and host migration remain future work.

The fault decorator also accepts REPLAY_JITTER in milliseconds and REPLAY_LOSS/REPLAY_DUPLICATE in packets per 10,000. Loss/duplication affect unreliable traffic; reliable ordering/delivery is preserved. For example:

Shell
REPLAY_JITTER=20 REPLAY_LOSS=1000 REPLAY_DUPLICATE=1000 \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/network_run.sh

The gameplay gate requires acknowledged delta traffic on every participant, alongside movement, action, state, and effect assertions.

The scripts set the collection root and scripts DLL path for the engine; the project has its own name and build outputs. REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 skips compilation only when running the acceptance gate against already current binaries.

Hello#

The script uses the shared game.Timeline runtime alias directly; generated Godot registration stays separate from the pure model package.

shared/hello/game.odin contains the complete simulation, shared with native tests: frame-owned actors, static kinematic collision, fire cooldowns, and projectile creation/expiry. scripts/hello.odin samples devices, advances fixed ticks, commits local results, and presents copies through replay/godot.

The offline Hello scene's second avatar is a stationary reference. Both avatars are player-controlled in the separate Network scene. Short button presses are buffered across render frames that produce no tick. Ordinary pause discards buffered gameplay edges and fixed-clock remainder. A control already held when pausing or resuming must be released before it can act again; presses made entirely while paused do not become deferred gameplay. Normal local state is immediately confirmed. Explicit playback rewind creates a fresh epoch from a retained frame; it does not rewrite already committed history inside the original epoch.

The test walks and fires using Godot's Input API, waits for projectile expiry, rewinds to a retained live-projectile frame, and verifies that its scene instance returns without replaying the historical muzzle effect. It also audits the real gameplay state after presentation.

Loot#

scripts/loot.odin imports the unchanged M1 loot model from godot:examples/replay_loot/game. This example therefore requires a repository checkout rather than only a packaged addon. It shows the blue player's predicted inventory transfer, then lets you correct the action to the orange player.

The complete world is revised; the presentation journal cancels the original take and begins the replacement while keeping the unchanged projectile effect. Repeated correction produces no duplicate effects. The fixture intentionally leaves that interaction unconfirmed and advances by commands for inspection.

Validation#

run.sh requires REPLAY_HELLO_OK and REPLAY_LOOT_VIEW_OK and rejects script errors, engine errors, and scenario failures. It builds on the engine-free tests/replay and tests/replay_view suites, including a WASM type-check of the instantiated view/clock/adapter/game surface. The broader input/history/recording acceptance now also runs real Chrome workflows. These are technical behavior checks, not a network comparison or a claim of human play-feel parity.

Set the scene’s debug_enabled inspector property or launch with REPLAY_DEBUG=1 for the local diagnostic overlay. F8 toggles the panel and F9 explicitly audits recent replayable history. It is disabled by default.

The same option enables the local history dock. F10 pauses for inspection; its slider paints retained frames without changing the live world. Resume keeps the original future, while Branch starts from the selected frame under a fresh presentation epoch. F8 can hide the audit panel while leaving the dock visible. Input held during inspection must be released before it controls the resumed game. This is an offline authoring workflow, independent of the network scene and the original Hello projects.

With REPLAY_DEBUG=1, F10 opens local history inspection. Choose a retained tick and a field, then Apply to preview. Reset or Resume discards edits; Branch starts from the edited frame. Game invariants are checked before accepting each edit. See ownership, supported values and limits.

The history dock also exports a portable recent recording: user://hello.rplrec on native (override with REPLAY_RECORDING_PATH), or a browser download. Export uses original history; preview edits are recorded after Branch. The separate headless verifier replays the file with Hello's shared model and reports the first mismatch.

Open recording loads a native .rplrec file or browser file selection. Play and the slider inspect recorded frames; Details shows verification results. Return to game restores the original pause, while Continue from recording starts a new local branch. Rejected replacements keep the previous loaded recording. See the playback ownership and limits.
